The noun first appears ONE VERSE PAST the row's close, plural and taken from those same messengers' hand, הַסְּפָרִ֛ים מִיַּ֥ד הַמַּלְאָכִ֖ים (oshb:Isa.37.14, byte), which contradicts the contrast rather than grounding it. The argument works in the English singular, “Hezekiah received the letter from the hand of the messengers” (web:Isa.37.14), and not in the Hebrew. (3) UNTIERED RECURRENCE - and STRONGER than the challenge tiered it. The two-token run אֱלֹהֵ֤י הַגּוֹיִם֙ (oshb:Isa.36.18, byte) recurs BYTE-IDENTICAL at exactly 2 verses book-wide (MT 36:18, MT 37:12; sweep: 2 verses). The minor gloss points hold: MT 37:14 reads the plural הַסְּפָרִ֛ים with a singular object suffix on the reading verb in the same run (oshb:Isa.37.14, byte) against WEB's “Hezekiah received the letter” (web:Isa.37.14); and its definite הַמַּלְאָכִ֖ים resolves the indefinite מַלְאָכִ֔ים of MT 37:9 (byte tier) across the row's opening seam. WHERE THE CHALLENGE OVER-FRAMES (the refinement): item (2)'s DIRECTIONAL FORCE. The challenge concludes that the tie 'argues continuity against the row's assertion of a self-contained rhetorical terminus'. That is not established. The anaphor sits INSIDE a fresh divine koh-amar frame - כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Isa.37.21, byte), one of the 44 divine-frame verses and a tier-1 seam signal - and an anaphoric back-reference under a NEW frame presupposes the prior unit is complete as readily as it argues continuation.
